openness.notes: Not officially documented; Gadgetbridge is the authoritative RE. The leojrfs writeup documents the Mi Band 2 auth handshake used here.

issued_to_client: The auth key (extracted from the official app on server-key devices)
credentials.notes: The 16-byte auth key gates control; on newer devices it is server- generated and must be extracted once from the official app. There is no Wi-Fi.
stored_on_device: 16-byte auth key (client-chosen on old bands, server-generated on newer)

factory_reset.effect: A reset (via the band's own menu or the official app) unbinds the band and rotates the auth key. Gestures vary by generation and are not transcribed here.

methods.description: Connect over BLE and run the three-step auth handshake on the auth characteristic with the 16-byte key. For server-key devices, extract the key once from the official app (e.g. from the app database / logs) before connecting.

steps.action: For server-key bands (Mi Band 4+), pair once in the official app and extract the auth key.
Connect, send {0x01,0x08,<key>} to the auth characteristic, request a random, and return AES-ECB(random).
steps.expect: A {0x10,0x03,0x01} success response authorises the session.

setup.notes: Older bands (1/1S/2) pair with a client-chosen key and need no cloud. Server-key devices (Mi Band 4/5/6/7, Amazfit Bip Lite, GTR, ...) require a one-time extraction of the auth key from the official app, after which control is offline. The extraction is an app/data step, not a wire step.

rejoin.notes: No network membership; re-authenticate with the key (or re-extract it after an app unpair).

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The Mi Band 2+ auth characteristic and three-step handshake are from the leojrfs writeup; the server-key extraction and per-generation notes are from Gadgetbridge's pairing documentation.

characteristics.notes: Three-step handshake: {0x01,0x08,<key>} then {0x02,0x08} then {0x03,0x08,AES-ECB(random)}; success is {0x10,<cmd>,0x01}.
